clauses.reason: The order's only operative command, "do order that the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry be amended accordingly and do hereby modify the Executive Order of December 9, 1933, approving said Code accordingly", approves a code of fair competition under section 3 of Title I of NIRA, and the approved code had legal effect only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The repeal therefore extinguished the prospective operative effect of the approval on June 14, 1935; the resolution states no later effective date, and no held record ends the approval earlier. The order amends the code and modifies the December 9, 1933 approval order (the held Executive Order 6487-B); the amendments the Federal Alcohol Control Administration recommended concern bottling without rectification and a ban on acquiring or selling spirits handled in violation of law, and operate only as terms of the amended code.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6685 of April 20, 1934 approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry and modifies the December 9, 1933 order approving that code, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA); its only operative command is that amendment and modification. The text states no period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval, and no held record cancels, suspends, supersedes or modifies the approval under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. The approval had legal effect only through section 3 (standards of fair competition under 3(b), equity enforcement under 3(c), misdemeanor liability under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, so the best supported first end of the approval's prospective operative effect is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end. Acts and liabilities before the repeal are accrued effects.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or modified under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. I read the order's full text (signed April 20, 1934; no stated period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval) and searched the held order texts for the code name and this order's number; the lookups report held later orders amend the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry code and recite the code as continuing (Executive Order 6812 of August 4, 1934, which recites this order by its date of April 20, 1934, and Executive Orders 6945 of January 10, 1935, 6954 of January 31, 1935, 7017 of April 19, 1935 and 7022 of April 20, 1935), and no held order cancels or supersedes the code. The WPA list entry for this order (1934 Apr 20, p.575) records the approval only. The OFR catalog starts in 1937, so it cannot show 1933-1935 endings, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the June 16, 1935 expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936. The machine report-deadline leads on this order's first paragraph are false positives: the words 'report recommending said amendments' describe a completed report in a recital, not a deadline. The later orders listed above amend the code and are later events, not ends of this order.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency, report requirement, committee or other command independent of the code amendment; its single command amends the code and modifies the earlier approval order.","savings_check":"Savings are the accrued effects described in the savings reason (S.J. Res. 113 and NIRA section 5 as held). The repeal's section 2 states no savings clause of its own; the held sources show no prosecution or enforcement continuing after June 14, 1935 and nothing that keeps the approval operative.","scope_check":"The inventory is the order's single clause, which covers the whole short text. The first paragraph (a Code Authority recommendation, a hearing by the Federal Alcohol Control Administration and its report recommending the amendments) is a recital. The operative command is the Now, Therefore paragraph, which adopts the report, orders the code amended and modifies the December 9, 1933 approval order accordingly. The order acts under Title I of NIRA, so the amendment and the modified approval rest on the section 3 power, and section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 reaches all of it."}

savings.reason: Fines, injunctions, convictions, liabilities and acts done under this code before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code taken before the repeal is likewise accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso, whose effect on pre-repeal action under codes the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, judgment: the code provisions in question were held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. Recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date; the delegation holding itself is in the opinion of the Court.
